response.sql: WITH sex_counts AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(DISTINCT e.ID) AS cnt FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.SEX), shares AS (SELECT sex, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share, AVG(cnt) OVER () AS avg_cnt FROM sex_counts), above AS (SELECT cnt, share, cnt - avg_cnt AS excess FROM shares WHERE cnt > avg_cnt) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: Examinations are matched to patients with an inner join on ID, so examinations with no matching Patient row are excluded.
NULL SEX and empty-string SEX are separate groups, as the request specifies, because GROUP BY keeps them apart.
Each sex's share is its distinct-patient count divided by the sum of all sex-group counts, and the per-sex average is the mean over all sex groups, including the blank and missing ones.
The 'average amount by which counts exceed the per-sex average' is the mean of (count - per-sex average) over the qualifying sexes, which are those with count strictly greater than that average.
